# From Deployment to Routine Science: Webb’s First Six Months

The James Webb Space Telescope was designed to fold into the Ariane 5 rocket’s fairing because its operational configuration was too large to fit inside. Unfolding it in space involved more than 50 major steps and over 300 possible single points of failure. The source notes that any one of them could have diminished or crippled the mission, and that repair was not possible at Webb’s distance from Earth.

By the second week, the secondary mirror and both wings of the primary mirror had unfolded and latched. Webb had reached its fully deployed operational configuration, but preparation for science continued. During the first month, the telescope and its instruments cooled for several weeks.

Mirror alignment took place in months two through four. Instrument-mode calibration followed in months five and six. Webb began routine science operations after six months.
